result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.remove_duplicate_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Remove duplicate edges, keeping only one edge per node pair. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1165-L1273){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.remove_duplicate_edges(keep_distinct_attributes=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each pair of nodes with multiple edges between them, keeps only the first edge (by edge ID order) and removes all others. This converts a multigraph into a simple graph with respect to multi-edges, but does not remove self-loops. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [keep_distinct_attributes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `False` (the default), edges are considered duplicates based solely on their source and target nodes, regardless of weight, `rel`, or other attributes. If `True`, edges with different attribute values (weight, `rel`, or custom attributes) are considered distinct and will not be removed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - by default, **edge attributes are ignored**: edges are considered duplicates based solely on their source and target nodes - use `keep_distinct_attributes=True` to preserve edges that have different weights, `rel` values, or other attributes - the first edge (lowest edge ID) in each group of true duplicates is retained - for directed graphs, edges `(u, v)` and `(v, u)` are considered different pairs - for undirected graphs, edges `(u, v)` and `(v, u)` are considered the same pair - does not remove self-loops (use `remove_selfloops()` or `simplify()` for those) - use `which_multiple()` to identify duplicate edges before removal - use `count_multiple()` to count duplicates per node pair before removal ## Examples {.doc-examples} By default, edges are considered duplicates purely by their endpoints, regardless of weight, so these three parallel "A"-"B" edges collapse down to one: ::: {#be81931b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=2.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=3.0) ) g.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: After calling `remove_duplicate_edges()`, only the first edge (lowest edge ID) survives: ::: {#6b9391cf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=2.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=3.0) .remove_duplicate_edges() ) g.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Setting `keep_distinct_attributes=True` treats edges with different attribute values as genuinely different, so only the true duplicate (the second "friend" edge) is removed: ::: {#e424bc6d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", rel="friend") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", rel="colleague") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", rel="friend") # true duplicate of the first edge .remove_duplicate_edges(keep_distinct_attributes=True) ) # "friend" and "colleague" both survive g.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: This is a typical step when merging data from multiple sources that may each report the same relationship: ::: {#cd1e52c5 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_edge(source="X", target="Y", type="email") .add_edge(source="X", target="Y", type="message") .add_edge(source="X", target="Y", type="call") .remove_duplicate_edges() ) g.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 1 ``` ::: :::
